title: Reconstruct Order From Arrow Hits
statement:
`n` soldiers stand in a single line, numbered by position `1` to `n` from the left. Each soldier wears a badge, an integer. A cannon on the left fires `n` arrows, one after another.

Arrow `i` (for `i = 1 ... n`) is described by two numbers `(d_i, a_i)`: at the moment it is fired, it kills the soldier who is currently standing at position `d_i` among the soldiers still alive (counted from the left, starting at `1`), and that soldier wears badge `a_i`. Whenever a soldier dies, every soldier behind him steps one place forward to fill the gap, so the positions of the survivors are renumbered before the next arrow.

After `n` arrows every soldier is dead. You are given all `n` arrows in the order they were fired. Reconstruct the original line-up and print the badges from left to right.

The input is always consistent: when arrow `i` is fired exactly `n - i + 1` soldiers are alive, and `1 ≤ d_i ≤ n - i + 1`. Badges are not necessarily distinct.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
Each of the next `n` lines contains two integers `d_i` and `a_i`, the arrows in the order they were fired.
outputFormat: Print `n` space-separated integers: the badges of the soldiers in the original line, from left to right.

examples.explanation: The original line is 20, 10, 30. Arrow 1 kills position 3 (badge 30), leaving 20, 10. Arrow 2 kills position 1 (badge 20), leaving 10. Arrow 3 kills position 1 (badge 10).
Work backwards. Start with an empty line and insert the last arrow's badge at its position: [5]. Then 9 at position 1: [9, 5]. Then 8 at position 2: [9, 8, 5]. Finally 7 at position 2: [9, 7, 8, 5].

hints: Run the process backwards: the last arrow kills the only soldier left, and each earlier arrow kills someone who was standing at position d_i in a longer line.
Going backwards, arrow i means: insert badge a_i at position d_i into the current line. Doing that with a plain list costs O(n) per insertion.

Instead, decide final slots directly. Arrow 1 takes slot d_1 of the final line, arrow 2 takes the d_2-th still-free slot, and so on. Find the k-th free slot with a Fenwick tree (binary lifting) or a segment tree.
